utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone that are in or just outside this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that both parties would have brief preliminary matters to raise. Mr. Stojanovic, Defence first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As briefly as possible, Your Honour, since we took it upon yourself yesterday I would just like to give you information about the exhibits that we used with Witness Milojica. At -- the Defence is not going to tender numbers 1D03024 and 1D30305 -- so 03025. And we stand by the proposal to tender into evidence 1D03628 and 1D4969. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is hereby on the record. One second, please. Yes, the documents you're not tendering, you tendered more or less in the 92 ter motion, but I do understand that you do not persist to that tendering. The Chamber will decide in due time on the remaining matters. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President, everyone. Regarding the document examiner's expert report, 65 ter 32125a, we have reviewed Mr. Ivetic's objection. We have, for several hours, reviewed the jurisprudence on this matter, and while we feel the situation as it came up in cross -- or excuse me, in direct and re-direct was rather unique. We feel that overall it is not worth or while to tender this document, and I am -- decided not do so and am withdrawing the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's hereby on the record. Mr. McCloskey, it was for exactly same reasons that the Chamber invited the parties to make written submissions rather than to deal with the matter immediately in court. You've decided how to proceed with it, and it's hereby on the record, and it saves the Defence some time. We have MFI'd the document under number P7148 and, therefore, that number is now vacated. If there's nothing else, is the Defence ready to call its next witness, which, as far as the Chamber understands, would be Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Perhaps, meanwhile, for the remaining two exhibits related to the -- associated exhibits in relation to Ratko Milojica there was no objection by the Prosecution. Therefore, 1D03628 would receive, Madam Registrar, number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 1D03628 will receive the number just vacated, which would be P7148.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Apologies, Your Honours. In that case it would be D911.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D911 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic. Please be seated. Mr. Dragutinovic, if you would allow us for a second to deal with a matter which we were in when you entered the courtroom, it will not take more than -- it will take less than a minute. Madam Registrar, could you assign a number to 1D04969.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number for 1D04969 will be D912.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D912 is admitted. Mr. Dragutinovic, you will first be examined by Mr. Stojanovic. You find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the record, I would like you to speak slowly and state your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Miodrag Dragutinovic. I was born on the 21st of March, 1950, in the village of Gojcin, municipality of Kalesija, Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm married. I have two children. I'm retired now. I'm a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us where it is that you live today?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I live in the neighbourhood of Celopek in the area of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the court about your professional training.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I completed a technical vocational school and I'm a land surveyor. I have a secondary education.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you have any kind of military education?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Your last question, the answer to your last question is found entirely in paragraph 1. The question you put to the witness invites him to tell us what is found in paragraph 2 of his statement. Let's try to avoid repetition, Mr. Stojanovic, and perhaps since the witness is a 92 ter witness, we could proceed with the attestation of his statement or --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we proposed to deal with this witness viva voce. That is what we announced, and we also stated the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I must have missed that, which I, depending on how it has reached us. If we missed it, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we asked for an hour and a half and we said viva voce. We're going to change the status of the witness, and I think we provided timely information on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll just try to find out -- I may have missed it. Perhaps my colleagues have missed it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we were informed of that, but there's not been created any sort of practice on getting the Judges to approve such a thing or not. So perhaps that would be more helpful because it does change things quite a bit when we go from one to the other, especially at the last minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll find out where we missed your information, if we missed any of that. Meanwhile, Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Dragutinovic, my last question was if you could tell us about your military education and training.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: When I did my regular military service, I completed the reserve officers' school in the engineering centre of Karlovac in Croatia. After completing this school, I was promoted to the rank of second lieutenant. Otherwise, this schooling went on for a year. So I now have the status of a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When the war started in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992, what was your status?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I was captain first class then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you join the Army of Republika Srpska at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In 1991 as a reserve officer, I was mobilised into the former JNA, and I remained there for about four months. After the JNA left Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 19th of May, 1992, all of us who were from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina stayed on in TO units, so I stayed on in a TO unit too. It was a unit at brigade level, in the Bijeljina garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that TO brigade with its headquarters in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the JNA it was called the 17th Majevica Brigade, and in the beginning of 1992 or, rather, after the JNA left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, after that agreement was reached, the unit that I stayed on in was the 1st Semberija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After the Army of Republika Srpska was established, did you join the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: After the Army of Republika Srpska was established, from the TO units, I was just promoted to member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what your duties were in terms of establishment and what unit you were in, in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the Semberija Brigade, I was in the operations department. I was a desk officer. And when I joined the Zvornik Brigade in August 1992, I was, yet again, a desk officer in the operations department.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you promoted at any point in time in terms of establishment as well?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, I was promoted assistant Chief of Staff for operations and teaching and otherwise I was promoted to the rank of major and that is the rank that I held until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the brigade where you were assistant Chief of Staff for operations and teaching?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The 1st Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think it may be better that the translation normally operations and training not teaching. I'm -- I'm sure the Defence would agree with that. It's just a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is. Because I do not know what the original language was. But, Mr. Stojanovic, training, teaching?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Literally it is operations and teaching. That's that work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, this is a -- as -- as the Court knows, a position in all brigades, corps, and the Main Staff, and it has always in this building been translated as operations and training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then it's clear how you understand it and that you -- of course, the Chamber is not in a position at this moment to say that -- not even knowing what the original language is, what was used, to have any comment on the translation, the interpretation of the words spoken by Mr. Stojanovic but you have drawn our attention to it, Mr. McCloskey, and I think we could leave it to that for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, this is what I'm interested in: In 1995, what did the personnel command structure of the Zvornik Brigade look like? Who was the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander was Lieutenant-Colonel Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff was Major - then - Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Formerly and according to establishment did he also carry out the duties of deputy commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander, how many assistant commanders did he have on the staff of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The commander had an assistant commander for morale; and assistant commander for security; and an assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have document 65 ter 05642 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, Mr. Stojanovic, could you briefly tell us exactly when the Chamber was informed that this was a viva voce witness? Because I -- the last thing I found was a message of the 23rd of February which gives corrections to the statement rather than announcing that it would be a viva voce witness. If you would have that available, then we can further verify what we missed, if we missed anything. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will check and I will tell you, Your Honour. At this point in time I'm not in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. McCloskey could also assist in telling us when he received the message because it may be that we then received the message as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we received that, the sheet that we're all familiar with of the schedule on 12 February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then on the 23rd of February, we receive a -- a correction to the statement which was ... what's the use of sending the Chamber information about the statement what is to be corrected what turned out during proofing if you're not using that statement at all, Mr. Stojanovic? And, Mr. McCloskey --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The reason -- the reason, Your Honour, was the practice that we had when examining the previous witness, when at one point in time, the Prosecution asked the Defence to say when it was that they had informed the OTP about Witness Jevdjevic having changed what he stated in his previous statement and we had the discussion about the two proofings regarding this witness who testified viva voce. After that decision of yours then I decided, out of an abundance of caution, to inform the Prosecution that the witness indicated to us a certain contradiction, if I can put it that way, between two paragraphs of this statement. So that is why I did that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine for the Prosecution. I don't think it affects the Chamber in any way if you don't want to use that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can tell you that these statements will be something that will be relevant and used in this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm -- yes. But that still doesn't resolve the initial matter which is, Mr. McCloskey, can you see anything that the Chamber was addressed in the message that was sent to you that the witness would be presented as a viva voce witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, our sheet shows viva voce, and Ms. Stewart is pointing me to Mladic case chamber so we do see you on the address list on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was exactly on what date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: 12 February, 1530 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We'll check that and see whether there's any communication problem within Chambers which, of course, we would immediately and seriously address if that's the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, perhaps you can clarify what you mean by the usual sheet. Do you mean the Defence exhibits for witness Dragutinovic, 92 ter/viva voce.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It is entitled, "Schedule of witnesses for week 16th or 19 February." It's got the boxes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yeah. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have, Mr. Stojanovic, are we supposed to if we have a 92 ter motion, which is not withdrawn, and if we get messages about what documents will be used, whether you will further stick to associated exhibits, et cetera, that we have to find on such a list without any further attention being given to it, without any further explanation to the Chamber, we have then to suddenly understand that this has become a viva voce witness. Is that the position of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. If it was our omission to inform you specifically, not only using this customary procedure, then it is an omission on our part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not a customary procedure. And, indeed, I found now the list the witnesses to be scheduled in the next upcoming weeks, and there it is said viva voce 1.5 hours but this is the only information we received. That is exactly the sheet which Mr. McCloskey was talking about. This has never come -- was never coming up before. This is not the normal procedure in this court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In addition, Mr. President, we have a witness schedule that was sent to the parties on 1 February 2015 where he was listed viva voce. But as I noted there has not been a process, which would be helpful, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, next time if you change that, don't provide us with a puzzle but provide us with clear, unambiguous information, because we spent a lot of time - we do - on preparing ourselves for the testimony of those witnesses, and we are not amused by being surprised in the way as you did. I find a document the 17th of February which still announced Mr. Dragutinovic as 92 ter/viva voce. That is two and a half weeks after you already apparently had decided not to call him as a -- not as a 92 ter motion. We further find -- let me just check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I refer to the 17th of February, it might be an error to that extent that it may be the date of the printing of that document. We'll carefully consider it, but I repeat, that we're not amused. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, in front of you, you see a schematic. I would kindly ask you to tell the Trial Chamber whether you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: This document shows the structure of command of the Zvornik Brigade. I was shown this document in 2001 when I provided my statement to the Tribunal's investigators. I signed it as my own, but I had some corrections to make. I believe that this document reflects the formation of the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to your position as the assistant Chief of Staff of operations and training, is it properly entered into this schematic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Within the system of command and control, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: It was the Chief of Staff. However, when it comes to the brigade structure, all the command members at any given moment could be subordinated to the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender 65 ter 05642.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 05642 receives number D913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D913 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, let's go back to the month of July of 1995. What was your specific task with regard to the military activities surrounding Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the military activities surrounding Srebrenica, the Zvornik Brigade received its task from the corps command. It was a preparatory order and it was received on the 2nd of July. On that same day, the brigade also received its combat order containing all the tasks for the units of the Zvornik Brigade. They were to be carried out in the Srebrenica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, can you tell the Trial Chamber what was the specific task of your own unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the combat order and before that in the preparatory order, the Zvornik Brigade received a task to establish a unit equalling a light battalion of up to 400 men and to be on stand-by until the 4th of July and to be ready to engage on its own independent axis. The axis was not specified at that moment, neither was the sector. In the combat order, however, those tasks were explained in detail, and we were fully aware of the tasks that the corps command had for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were those specific tasks that your unit was assigned?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: As part of the combat order, in its first part - and the combat order was issued by the command of the Drina Corps - we were told about the intentions and the tasks assumed to be undertaken by the enemy. Also the tasks and assessments of the command of the Drina Corps as to what to do in order to prevent any activities of the 2nd Corps of the BiH Army. And after that, tasks for the units, including the units of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to call up 65 ter 04293.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand what the tasks of this unit were from that last answer, and I know have you persisted to try and find out what they were. Are you satisfied that you've got the tasks now?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will continue exploring operative tasks when the next document is displayed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a form of leading where you asked someone for the tasks and then show him the tasks. It's not a particularly -- matter of -- of being contested, but he did not answer the question about the tasks and now we see the order that lists the tasks. So I think it would be best for the question to be answered before the document is shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I consider this to be a general observation about leading questions, Mr. Stojanovic, without any direct consequences for this matter which apparently is not in dispute. But it's not for the first time that the technique of questioning witnesses in examination-in-chief has been raised, and I would like you to pay more attention to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. And you will see that the document that we have on the screen does not suggest anything and does not speak about those tasks. However, I am happy to entertain your objection about leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in front you, there is an order. Could you please look at paragraph 1. My first question: What is this about? What kind of an order is this?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: This is a preparatory order of the command of the Zvornik Brigade to establish a unit that will be engaged in the Srebrenica combat sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to this tactical group that was to be established by the Zvornik Brigade, who were its members?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the combat order of the corps command, and I understand that a minute ago that I did not provide a full answer about its tasks and I intend to answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll come back to that. Could you please answer my previous question first.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Brigade, pursuant to that order, received the task to establish a unit equalling a light battalion and based on that order, the Zvornik Brigade took into account the intention of the commander and I drafted the document and elaborated it. Indeed, it did establish a tactical group, that was Tactical Group 1. That's what we called it. In this order, we explain how that tactical group should be composed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one question. To the best of your recollection how many men did Tactical Group 1 have?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Tactical Group 1 did not have more than 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My next question, as can you see in this document, there is reference to the armoured mechanised company. What was it composed of?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The tactical group was based on two combat groups. One combat groups was formed of a mobile unit from the Zvornik Brigade, a detachment which was a reserve unit for active combat. And combat group 2 which was established and had a temporary composition. Its members came from the battalion of the brigade, whereas the armoured mechanised company was attached to the tactical group as support and consisted of four tanks, four APCs, one anti-aircraft cannon Praga, as well as two Strela-2M to protect the armoured mechanised company against an air strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now could you please tell the Trial Chamber what was the specific task of your tactical group, which is Tactical Group 1 in respect of Srebrenica? Could you please first answer the previous question, i.e., what was the general task of the units that were deployed in the sector of Srebrenica. Go ahead tell us and then answer my last question as well.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the preparatory order of the command of the Drina Corps and later the combat order of the Drina Corps the task of the unit that were deployed and were to be deployed in the Srebrenica sector was for the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa to be separated from each other and to narrow down the manoeuvre space of the 28th Division which was in the protected area of Srebrenica, as well as the protected area of Zepa. That brigade had not been demilitarised, had not been disarmed. It was well equipped and in the spring of 1995 based on all the intelligence, it was well prepared for combat. Its task, according to all the assessments, was to be used as a unit which would act from the sector of the protected areas of Srebrenica and Zepa in concert with the other units and attack all the units of the Drina Corps. Those other units were the units of the 2nd Corps which were to attack the Drina Corps and the ultimate goal was for the units of the BiH army to get to the Drina river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the specific task within the overall strategic task of Krivaja 95? What was the specific task of your Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The task of Tactical Group 1 pursuant to the Drina Corps order which was later elaborated, was to deploy units to the Zeleni Jadar sector, to get to the separation line, Bukova Glava-Javor-Zeleni Jadar and to launch an attack along the axis Zeleni Jadar, Pusmulic village, Bojne. The more specific task was to dispel the enemy forces on the axis of the attack and to get to the Rajne village-Zivkovo Brdo line. And the next task was to get to the Bojne village sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender 65 ter 04293 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 04293 receives number D914.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, when you arrived in the sector that was assigned to you pursuant to this task, when was that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The unit was set up on the 4th of July. We marched to the Srebrenica sector in two columns. One column consisted of the armoured mechanized company. They started marching along the Zvornik-Bratunac line and got to the Pribicevac sector on that same day, on the 4th of July, and the rest of the tactical group marched along the Bratunac-Zvornik-Skelani axis and they spent the night in Jezera village and then in the morning of the 5th of July, they arrived in the Zeleni Jadar sector.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down, especially when enumerating all the villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially if you list names, could you please slow down but also in general, could you slow down your speed of speech. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now could you please tell the Trial Chamber when the combat of Tactical Group 1 started?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Drina Corps order for tactical -- for combat activity, combat started on the 6th of July early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any specific orders regarding UNPROFOR observation points along the axis of movement of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On that axis, there was an observation point in the Biljeg feature sector. That was along the axis of movement of Tactical Group 1 of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any specific instructions as to how you should treat UNPROFOR members at that observation point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We all knew what the function of UNPROFOR was. Our task was to let UNPROFOR do their job and that we should try not to disturb them or engage in any other way against the UNPROFOR observation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to this observation point, what was the position of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: That gave rise to a problem which escalated later when the UNPROFOR units left the Biljeg observation point and the problem was as follows: On the left and on the right from the UNPROFOR observation point, some 50 to 100 metres away, there were defence positions of the 28th Division so that the observation point was effectively along the line and part of the defence of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did it come a time when you had to engage the crew of the UN observation point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether you had any specific orders with regard to the civilian population, should you had any encounters with them within the combat area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In any case, the standing order was that the objective of our combat activities were not civilians, was not the enclave, or UNPROFOR units. Our objective was exclusively the 28th Division which was a permanent danger for the units of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were engaged in combat, did you actually have encounters with the civilian population from the enclave?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not have any direct contact with them. However, from our reconnaissance position, and that was the reconnaissance position of the Howitzer detachment of Tactical Group 1 which was our tactical group, we could see the movements of the civilian population as soon as combat started. The civilian population was moving along the axis Slapovic, left to the units of Tactical Group 1, across Bajramovic, towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Court in this courtroom to the best of your recollection how things followed after that, from the 6th until the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 6th of July, the units of the tactical group were not very successful. They took part of the features on the axis of attack. They had a certain number of wounded. And in view of the result, the commander of the tactical group, Tactical Group 1, Vinko Pandurevic, he stopped combat activities. He called in the commanders of the tactical groups and made a decision to group forces and the tactical group was supposed to attack along the axis Javor-Biljeg-Ravne. The task envisaged was supposed to take place on the next day in the early morning hours. That is, the 7th of July. The units were gathered there, taken from positions and gathered there, and prepared for combat activities in the morning hours of the 7th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What were the results of this combat?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning hours of the 7th of July, combat activities did not start because there was a lot of rain and fog so this attack was postponed until the weather conditions got better. The weather conditions did not get better all the way up until the 8th, the afternoon of the 8th, when the units started their attack, and struck forcefully, came to the Biljeg area and to the left arrived at the forested elevations that we in our own jargon called Tri Sise these are dominant features above the road from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica, that is to say, just above the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened in the battlefield on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, on the 9th of July, we continued combat activities and reached the line Rajne-Zivkovo Brdo. That was the closer task from the order of the Drina Corps. On the 10th in the early morning hours, the 28th Division carried out a counter-attack, pushed back our forces to the area of Biljeg, Tri Sise or, rather, above the road Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica and that is where we consolidated and prepared for a counter-attack of our own in an attempt to get back to the line that had been reached the previous day, that is, the line Rajne-Zivkovo Brdo. In the afternoon hours on the 10th, we took again the hill that we had lost, Zivkovo Brdo, and we got to the village of Rajne on the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica road and there by we carried out this more immediate task from the command of the Drina Corps. Afterwards, according to the situation that was very favourable for us, combat activities continued, and we got to the Bojne line and that was the next task from the combat task issued by the command of the Drina Corps. Thereby our task was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get a new combat task at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I can add that to the left Since Tactical Group 1 was on the main axis of attack, there was Tactical Group 2 that was operating and it was somewhat less successful so we had to wait for them to reach the lines that they were given by the command of the Drina Corps. So in the afternoon hours of the 10th, we received the task of preparing on the following day, the 11th of July, continuing combat activities along the Bojne-Srebrenica-Gostilj-Potocari road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who issued that order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours of the 10th, in the area of Bojna, General Krstic arrived there and he gave us the basic tasks. The following day, they were spelled out in more concrete terms and materialised.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, did you set out to accomplish the next task that you were given by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Units prepared to continue combat activities -- excuse me. Then around midday, units started their axis of attack along the Bojne-Srebrenica-Gostilj-Potocari road, and, at that moment, just before combat started and somewhat after that, NATO aircraft carried out strikes against the units of Tactical Group 1 in the area of Bojna. However, this did not distract the unit of the Zvornik Brigade and other units and did not stop them from carrying out their tasks further.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tactical Group 1, was it affected by the NATO bombing in any way?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Combat vehicles were destroyed and one ambulance and one command vehicle of the commander of Tactical Group 1, the commander of the Podrinje detachment and then one truck that contained a certain amount of ammunition. There weren't any other effects.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally affected by the NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: During the second NATO air-strike, I was near the damaged vehicles. These combat vehicles -- well, practically were not combat vehicles. It was an ambulance, a command vehicle, and a truck. They were bombed yet again. Since I was nearby, when the missiles hit, the anti-armour missiles, I suffered a minor contusion. At first, I didn't have any particular consequences.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you personally go after this contusion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: After a while, certain symptoms appeared, namely, headaches, vomiting, dizziness. Commander Vinko Pandurevic suggested that I be take to our logistics units in the Zeleni Jadar area in an ambulance. We had a medical post there and then a doctor could see me and see what the consequences were and perhaps could send me to Zvornik for further examinations and medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, just one more question. That afternoon and evening on 11th July 1995, how far did Tactical Group 1 get?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: One can say that except for the 10th and the 8th, 9th, 11th, before the units of Tactical Group 1 from the Zvornik Brigade got there, there was no particular resistance in Srebrenica itself and very quickly the line that was involved in the task was reached. And that was when arriving at the line to the left of Gostilj, I think 522 is the feature, and on the right-hand side there was another elevation and that is where the group was supposed to stop and spend the night or, rather, be ready for continuing combat activities in accordance with the order of the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it seems to me that it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is time for the break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, coming briefly to what happened before, this witness, Mr. Dragutinovic, was presented in your Rule 65 ter witness list as a 92 ter witness. On the 1st of February, he was still presented as a 92 ter/viva voce witness. The same happened on the 6th of February, 92 ter and viva voce. It was only on the 12th of February that he appears on one of your lists without any further explanation as a viva voce witness. Now, whether you would need leave to change your 92 ter witness list is a matter that could be discussed, but at least it is -- whether the witness is a 92 ter witness or a viva voce witness, clearly appears in the information you have to provide under Rule 65 ter (G) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Now, adding an exhibit to the 65 ter list, you need certainly leave for that. Whether you would need leave to change the status of a witness is a matter that could still be discussed, but there can be no doubt that if you change the status of a witness on your Rule 65 ter list that at least a clear and unambiguous announcement must be given, which has not been done in this case. I hereby instruct you that whenever a similar status, change of status is envisaged by the Defence, that even before announcing the change that the Chamber should be informed about that intention so that the Chamber can, if it wishes to do so, further comment on it. Let that be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And apart from that, Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any intention to withdraw your 92 ter motion, which you haven't done. I mean, if you present a witness as viva voce, wouldn't it be appropriate then to withdraw in, again, unambiguous terms, that you withdraw your 92 ter motion. Yes. I was able to figure this out just in a couple of minutes, Mr. Stojanovic. You had three weeks to figure that out. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one small unrelated issue. I think there's been a translation issue. The witness I believe it was page 24 mentioned from that the NATO bombing he suffered a contusion. I believe that that may be concussion. It's always been concussion before so I don't know if he's changed words or not. But I just alert that because it does have some significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, talking about translations, I noticed, Mr. McCloskey, in the statement which we are supposed not to have read, the 92 ter statement given by the witness, that the "training" is the word rather than "teaching." And I take it that this is a translation of the same words as used here in court when the witness was questioned on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think that's probably right, though, of course, I don't know the word he used. If he -- but as an officer, I'm sure he got the right word, I would think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the reason I said, "I take it, it's not a certainty." Mr. Stojanovic, if there's anything you'd like to tell us now, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, two things. So, yes, we withdraw our proposal for Witness Dragutinovic to be heard in accordance with Rule 92 ter. We stand by the proposal to hear him viva voce. From that point of view, we changed his status. And we have also taken note and I believe that in the future there will be other situations like that. We are going to inform you not only through the witness list of their status but for each and every concrete case, we are going to provide timely information on the change of status. And that is the practice that we are going to follow in the future, along with our apologies for not having done it now, specifically but only through this motion of the 12th of February, in terms of how the witness is going to be examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, perhaps you carefully re-read your own -- the language you used. I think whatever language you used the matter is sufficiently clear to the Chamber. But I would specifically draw your attention to where you said "we are going to provide timely information on the change of status." Precise language would have been "we are going to provide timely information on our intention to change the status." We take a break, and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, we were talking about the 11th of July and what happened in the afternoon on that day. When -- where did you spend the night between the 11th and the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I spent that night in the logistics unit, i.e., in the medical unit of Tactical Group 1 in the Zeleni Jadar sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July in the afternoon, did you communicate with Pandurevic who was the commander of tactical group?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening on the 11th, the commander arrived in the Zeleni Jadar sector and he gave us our basic task and that was for the logistic unit to move certain equipment as quickly as possible to the Srebrenica sector as well as to the Gostilj sector where units of the Tactical Group 1 were. We were to prepare to spend the night on the positions reached. At the same time, he wanted to see me as his operative officer to inquire about my medical condition because I had refused to go to Zvornik for further checkups and treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, on the 12th, in the morning, what was the axis of your movement?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, on the 12th of July, the logistics base in Zeleni Jadar was again visited by the commander. He gave us our task and that was for the logistics organs, the whole logistics and everything that belonged to it, to move to the Srebrenica sector as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally head for Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since the physician provided the commander with his opinion, I insisted that I could return to the unit without any particular consequences. As a result of that, together with the commander, I returned to Srebrenica on the 12th, sometime between 9.00 and 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you and Mr. Pandurevic travel from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the command vehicle of the commander of Tactical Group 1, Mr. Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Pandurevic tell you anything about his movements the previous evening on the 11th and during the night between the 11th and the 12th?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Given our relationship, him as a commander and me as an operative, it was only logical that I was kept abreast of the situation in the unit and possible task, as well as the movements of the commander and his intentions. Therefore, he told me that on the 11th, in the evening and later during the night he had had a briefing or a debriefing in the command of the Bratunac Brigade and that he had returned very late and that he had taken a different route to the one that he had taken from Srebrenica to Bratunac, i.e., from Srebrenica to Bratunac, he travelled in the command vehicle and he took the route Srebrenica-Potocari-Bratunac. In the Potocari sector, he encountered a large group of people; men, women, and children. He realised that he had a mistake to take that route but it was too late already and he managed to negotiate his way to Bratunac somehow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the route that he took on the way back?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since his estimate was that he would have threatened the lives of the people in the vehicle, i.e., the driver and two soldiers from his protection unit and because of his own personal safety, he took a different route and that was Bratunac-Sase-Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who attended that debriefing on the 11th of July in the evening at the command of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We did not discuss the debriefing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That has no foundation. It may be what did you learn or who told you, but unless he establishes that this person was there, that's an improper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited to lay a basis for the knowledge of the witness about the debriefing on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the commander, Pandurevic, tell you what the debriefing at the command of the Bratunac command was about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Basically what I learned from the commander was that the debriefing was about previous combat activities and the future task which was established at that meeting. And that was that the units were to be deployed in the Zepa sector to engage the Zepa Brigade and neutralise its members. As for the rest of that meeting, I really don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about the participants of the debriefing. Who was there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you arrived Srebrenica on the 12th, when did you arrive, to the best of your recollection and estimate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: It was sometime between 10.00 and 11.00, but it would sooner be closer to 10.00 than closer to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that your first arrival in Srebrenica during the war?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my first arrival in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What did you find there in Srebrenica, in terms of facilities?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The town itself was a sore sight. I had known Srebrenica from before as a small tourist place, and I live in a similar town, but it was in a -- a state of disarray. However, there were no signs of destruction. I could not observe any signs of previous combat in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find any civilians there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the town itself, apart from the units, there were no civilians at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was your next combat task? How was it worded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just add when I arrived in Srebrenica while we were still in the vehicle, the commander emphasised that he expected or he was awaiting an order for further use of our unit. As soon as we arrived in the Gostilj sector, where our command was located, the task did arrive, indeed, so we started to prepare our unit for the accomplishment of that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How was it worded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The task, in short, would be the following: Tactical Group 1, headed by Commander Pandurevic was supposed to be reserved for Tactical Group 2 which would scout the terrain along the axis Srebrenica-Viogor-Suceska. It was to move behind Tactical Group 2 in a marching order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, did you embark on carrying out that task?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Already around 12.00 units of the Zvornik Brigade, i.e., of the Tactical Group 1 were prepared to start marching along the axis Srebrenica-Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did that engagement last?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived there around 1500 hours. Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any encounters with the elements of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Tactical Group 2, which marched in front of the Zvornik Brigade, did not come in contact with parts of the 28th Division. We informed our command about that, and we continued moving in a column along the Viogor pass axis. This means that Tactical Group 2 was also not in contact with parts of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And during that afternoon, on the 12th of July, did any of the officers visit you on the positions reached?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Before I answer your question, I'd like to add that one of the elements of the task was this: When your units arrive at the Siljato Brdo-Viogor sector, they should get ready and start moving towards the Suceska village sector in a combat order because there assumptions based on intelligence that elements of the 28th Division were concentrated there. As we arrived in the Viogor sector from the intelligence organ, we received intelligence and we were also informed by the Drina Corps that in the Suceska sector there were no elements of the 28th Division. We were thus ordered to stay there, both Tactical Group 2 and Tactical Group 1 in the Viogor sector, and to await our further orders there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was it who gave you your further orders?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours on the 13th -- or, rather, the 12th of July, the 12th of July, I apologise. It was on the 12th of July. General Krstic arrived in the Viogor sector. In view of the situation that prevailed ahead of us, he gave us our task, and that was to get ready to start marching in the direction of the Zepa enclave. He also told us that the -- the details of that task would be specified on the following day, i.e., on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night between the 12th and the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The whole unit, Tactical Group 1 together its command, spent the night in the Viogor sector. We had set up our command there, as well as all the other elements that are needed for a unit to spend the night in the open. We set up security and all the other elements that were needed to secure the unit under such circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did any of the elements of the tactical group or the Zvornik Brigade on that day, on the 12th of July, have any specific tasks in the Potocari sector?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, units of the Zvornik Brigade did not receive any tasks. They did not receive any orders with regard to the Potocari sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, the 13th of July, in the morning, did you have an opportunity to meet with any of your superior officers?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, around 10.00 in the morning, the Viogor sector where the units of Tactical Groups 1 and 2 were camping, was visited by General Mladic, General Krstic. I don't remember whether there were any other members of the superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And on that occasion, did General Mladic address your unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: General Mladic addressed the troops and unit commands. He delivered a short speech. In military terminology, that would be called a speech, but it was rather to inform us about the situation on the -- in the theatres of war of the Herzegovina, Sarajevo-Romanija, and East Bosnia Corps. He gave us an overview of the situation -- situation and combat activities in Serbian Krajina. After that, he gave us a specific task.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And that task was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: That task was, in short, that unit commanders should gather their units to provide them with material and technical equipment and that they should start marching in the direction of the Zepa sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any suggestions by the subordinated officers with regard to that task?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Usually after a task is issued by a commander of a superior command, and in that specific case, it was our Supreme Commander, General Mladic, no objections are ever expected. The only thing that is expected was for General Mladic was to ask whether everybody was clear on the task or whether there were any dilemmas with regard to the accomplishment of the task. The commander of Tactical Group 1, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko Pandurevic, asked permission to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What did Mr. Pandurevic say on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since General Mladic allowed Vinko Pandurevic, the commander of the tactical group, to present his position, Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic, as far as I can remember, provided a short analysis which consisted in the following: He said that basically we had not dispelled or broken up the 28th Division, that the 28th Division had only moved into the north -- northern part of Srebrenica enclave where they were deployed around Jaglici village sector and he said that most probably they would try to break through across the territory controlled by the Army of Republika Srpska along the Konjevic Polje-Udrc-Kamenica-Baljkovica axis and that axis was most commonly used by them when they infiltrated independent units of the 28th Division. As soon as they came behind the back of the Zvornik Brigade, i.e., the 7th, 4th and 6th battalions, i.e., left of Memici, across Baljkovica to Petkovci. That meant that the defence of the Zvornik Brigade would be threatened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic and Mr. Witness, especially Mr. Witness, you should slow down while speaking. It is very complicated for the interpreters to follow. And please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember, whether, on that occasion, General Mladic said something or answered in some way, whether he said anything in response to what Pandurevic had said?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, General Mladic basically said the following: The corps command has sufficient forces that would stop the 28th Division from crossing the Konjevic Polje-Kasaba-Milici road and with regard to that question, the commander of the tactical group Vinko Pandurevic should not have any concerns and that he has his basic task and that he should set out to accomplish that task. Commander Vinko Pandurevic as an officer said, Yes, sir, General, and that is how the conversation ended, that is to say, this conversation between the general and Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was any mention of the civilian population in the enclave on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian population, as far as I can remember, was not mentioned at all. It was only military affairs, the 28th Division, its position, the position of our units, and the tasks that were to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any mention of any possible POWs?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive at your new position in accordance with the combat task received?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived at the new position in the morning hours around 2.00 on the 14th of July in the area of the village of Pozeplje or, rather, the village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any combat activities or any movement of your tactical group on that day, the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, upon arriving in the area of Pozeplje and receiving a task from the corps command, the command of the tactical group elaborated this concrete task and set out to carry it out. This is what it consisted of: In the Pozeplje-Plana area, I think that's the name of the village, along the road Brloznik-Purtici-Cavici, an attack was supposed to be carried out, and in accordance with the task the line in the village of Purtici should be reached. Further on along the Purtici-Cavici road, the line should be reached in the village -- at this moment I simply cannot remember. I think it was east of the village of Cavici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any combat on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: There was combat in the village of Brloznik where there were no inhabitants at all. Then after that fighting continued a bit towards the village of Cavici where it stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any casualties on either side?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We had some wounded. There weren't any persons who got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell the Court where you spent the night between the 14th and 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The unit spent the night at the positions reached and the command of the tactical group spent the night in the school in the village of Pozeplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after the 15th of July in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since the units were already prepared in the early morning hours of the 15th to continue their activities along the Purtici-Cavici-Zepa road the command of the tactical group had already reached the units when the commander received a call from the forward command post, the village of Krivace, from General Krstic, to call the forward command post, the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the next task?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: After the commander returned from the forward command post, and he went there about 8.00 and he returned about 9.00, with the approval of General Krstic, the units of the Zvornik Brigade because of the situation that was going on at that moment in the rear of the Zvornik Brigade, at the Memici-Baljkovica road, Petkovci, he allowed that the units from the tactical group from the Zvornik Brigade could return to their original units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to the best of your recollection when it was that you returned to the area of Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: After the units of the tactical group withdrew from the positions attained, a column was formed and the commander awaited for that. And then at the helm of the column, he set out in the direction of Zvornik and he gave me the task that within the armoured mechanised company, I should be at the rear end of that column.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, when was that you arrived in the area of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I arrived in the area of the Zvornik Brigade around 14, 1500 hours, the area Zlatne Vode. That's on the old road between Zvornik and Tuzla, on the outskirts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you receive your next order -- task from and what was it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Before leaving, the commander gave me a task stating that I should stay in Zlatne Vode and wait for replenishment of the unit. The replenishment did arrive in Zlatne Vode --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the commander sent this to me through him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat where the replenishment did arrive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The replenishment arrived in Zlatne Vode. That is on the outskirts of the town of Zvornik on the old road between Zvornik and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you act on this order; and where did you find yourself on the afternoon of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The order stated that within the armoured mechanized company, I should set out along the Zlatne Vode-Caparde-Memici road with the following task: To support the 7th Battalion and control the road that from Tuzla, via Memici and Caparde, leads to Zvornik, that I should hold it using my own fire-power and parts of the unit should support the 7th Battalion in fighting the units that were attacking from the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any intelligence about the strength of the enemy, the 28th Division of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the combat order of the command of the Drina Corps, it said that the 28th Division consisted of five brigades and the sixth one was the Zepa Brigade. The estimate was that in it there are between 4 to 5.000 armed soldiers. The strength of the column, we could assume that, but one could take it as correct that there were between 4 to 5.000 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information as to which units of the Army of Republika Srpska - and possibly attached units - were in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The 7th Battalion in the area of Memici. The 4th, in the area of Baljkovica. The 6th, in the area of Dugi Dio, Petkovci. They were defending Memici on the left and Petkovci on the right, and then in depth, part of the units in that area, on the 15th upon our arrival, the Podrinje detachment was already there that is to say from our tactical group, and then part of Tactical Group 2, from the tactical group, then a company from the Bratunac Brigade, a platoon from the Vlasenica Brigade, then a company of the special brigade of the police from Zvornik. One company of the special brigade of the police from Sekovici, and I think one company from the special police brigade from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That night, between the 15th and the 16th, did combat ensue between these units that you mentioned and the enemy units?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The main fighting took place between the units of the 2nd Corps of the BiH army that were attacking at the lines of defence of the 7, 4th, and partly 6th Battalion, with the intention of carrying out a breakthrough through the defence lines of the mentioned battalions and to link up with the 28th Division or, rather, parts of it. And thereby make it possible to get them out of the positions that they were in. However, these attacks on the 15th did not yield fruit, so the units of the 2nd Corps or, rather, parts of it, did not get through the defence line and did not link up with the 28th Division, so the 28th Division found itself in a rather unenviable position, in view of our knowledge to the effect that there were many civilians within it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the intensity of that combat on the basis of the experience that you had in the years of war up until then?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since I was on the left flank of the actual battlefield within the 7th Battalion, I could visually, directly, and partly via radio communications, I could follow all developments in the Baljkovica area. In the briefest possible terms, this is what it boils down to. In the early morning hours, on the 16th, sometime around 4.00, the units of the 2nd Corps carried out a very strong intensive attack against the positions of the 7th Battalion and the fiercest attack was against the positions of the 4th Battalion and partly the 6th Battalion that was linked with the 4th Battalion along the Baljkovica river. They managed, in part, to disrupt the defence of the 4th Battalion and afterwards that was repaired as the Podrinje detachment came in. So on the 16th of July, the units of the 2nd Corps of the Army of BiH did not break through the lines of the 4th Battalion and were not able to assist parts of the 28th Division and the civilians that were right behind them. Whoever is familiar with that area, that terrain, can just imagine the 28th Division, the civilian part that was moving towards them since they did not have any help and they did not receive any help from the units of the 2nd Corps, of course, in combat terms, they found themselves in a cauldron and on that morning, we say in our language it is boiling like it is in a cauldron. That was the intensity of the combat activities. During those five years of war, I had not experienced that kind of intensity in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you've got a few minutes left. Could I remind you of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope I will be able to finish, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, in view of the history of this testimony, that we might be rather strict. And then I've not yet in any way calculated the time we wasted on the matter, you still remember, from before the break, so you get the full net one hour and a half, and that's it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, try to shorten your answers so I may be able to use the time that remains.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to hear that an agreement could be reached between the two parties in order to overcome the situation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: From the commander of the battalion, I was keeping abreast of the situation. In view of the situation in the Baljkovica sector, Commander Vinko Pandurevic upon the insistence of the other side, through Colonel Semso Muminovic was involved in the negotiations with a view to overcoming the situation which had escalated that morning. The commander of the Zvornik Brigade and the -- the other side thought that it would be opportune to cease-fire and that was indeed what happened and then the next step was to see how the 28th Division could withdraw together with the situation how they could overcome the situation that they encountered in the cauldron in the Baljkovica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to that agreement, how long did this cease-fire last; and how long did the corridor remain open?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The agreement was that combat activities would be interrupted around 10.00 and that the cease-fire should last until the 17th, around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you honour the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Both sides fully honoured the agreement which was reached between Commander Pandurevic and Colonel -- and the colonel from the 2nd Corps of the BiH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody from the superior command come to the area to see what the situation was like?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th in the afternoon, I found myself in the Baljkovica sector. My task was to surveil the situation because the cease-fire was to end and the corridor was to be closed. One part of the detachment also arrived in the Baljkovica sector. Their task was together with the 4th battalion unit that I had brought was to close that corridor. I learned that three officers from the Main Staff had spent some time at the IKM. Their task was to learn about what had happened the previous day and earlier that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your previous answer, and that was that you visited the scene where the corridor was opened, did you have an opportunity to see the casualties of the previous intense fighting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: My task was to co-ordinate my activities with the company that had arrived in the sector of the 7th Battalion to enter the defence sector of the 7th Battalion not in a combat order but just to observe the situation. I was not to scour the terrain. I was to ascertain whether any units had been infiltrated by the 7th Corps. When I arrived in the Baljkovica sector I see there was no such unit. I got in touch with the battalion and with the detachment, and I accomplished the task of closing the corridor. I could see as much as the time allowed me to see. I could see the scene of the battle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, your time is over. If you have one last question, you with put it to the witness, but when I warned you a couple of minutes ago that the time was very limited, you just continued to listen to evidence which, for example, your last question has not been answered by the witness. He expends a lot of time on matters which are -- we still do not know whether he had an opportunity to see the casualties, because that was the question, and you let him go for minutes and minutes. Apparently that's the way in which you wish to use your time in examination-in-chief. If you have one last question to the witness, you may put it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, my last question. Did you observe any wounded or any other casualties of the intense fighting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I saw dead bodies. I didn't see any wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragutinovic, on behalf of the Mladic Defence, I would like to thank you for the answers you provided to us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this brings the examination-in-chief of this witness to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we move on to the cross-examination, I have one or two questions I'm seeking clarification. I'll take you back to the 11th of July, Witness. You know, that's the day when you were transported and saw the doctor and where you said you stayed overnight, I think, it was in Zeleni Jadar, and it was on that same day that quite -- that the debriefing took place on which you were questioned extensively. One of the questions was, and that was before Mr. McCloskey intervened. The question was: "Who attended that debriefing on the 11th of July in the evening at the command of the Bratunac Brigade? " And then your answer was: "We did not discuss the debriefing." And you were talking about your conversations with Mr. Pandurevic. That was your answer. Then when asked that was the next question: "Did the commander, Pandurevic, tell you what the debriefing at the command of the Bratunac command was about?" And then you told us what you learned from Pandurevic. Now what I do not understand yet is that on the one hand, you say, We did not discuss the debriefing, and, on the other hand, you tell us what you learned from Mr. Pandurevic about the debriefing. Could you explain that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way I understood the question was this: Didn't Mr. Pandurevic tell me who had attended the meeting or the debriefing besides him? And I said that Mr. Pandurevic did not tell me who exactly had attended that debriefing. So I really don't know who had attended. I can only assume but it would be nothing but an assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
