utterances.text: Your answer reads differently. Your answer reads: "We did not discuss the debriefing." But I now understand that you intended to say that he didn't tell you who attended that debriefing. Now, before he went there, did he tell you who had called that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usually it would be the commander of the superior units. Therefore -- please allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Witness. I'm interrupting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you who usually would do that. I asked you whether Pandurevic told you who had called that meeting. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told me that a meeting was called by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not General Mladic. It was General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, by -- as -- due to an unfortunate development of procedural events, this Chamber had -- has looked at a statement which is not in evidence, and in that statement in paragraph 13 I read -- and it's a statement which was signed by you, and I'll just read the one line which is relevant. You said in that statement: "I stayed the night between 11 and 12 July while Pandurevic left Srebrenica for Bratunac, travelling via Potocari. He said he was going to a meeting called by Generals Mladic and Krstic ..." My question to you is: What now explains that in that statement which you signed, a statement which was corrected later but not in this respect, that suddenly it is reported that you said that the meeting was called by Generals Mladic and Krstic; whereas, you now say, No, he told me that it was Krstic. And what explains that you did not correct that when you were briefed recently? When -- I used the wrong expression; during proofing sessions recently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I said during my first testimony in 2007 what I said it is quite possible that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you there again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was not about your testimony in 2007. My question was about what you told us a minute ago, comparing that with a statement which reflects -- which was signed by you in July 2014 and reflects interviews held in June and October 2013, during which you are reported to have said - and you signed for that - that the meeting was called by Generals Mladic and Krstic. Do you have any explanation why you signed that statement and why you did not correct that recently during proofing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would have stood by the statement that I provided previously, and that is that the meeting was called by Generals Mladic and Krstic. So what I'm saying now, i.e., the current statement, I could - how should I put it? - I could change that. Not in the sense that I'm changing the meaning of the statement but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. You stay you stand by your signed statement that the meeting was called by Generals Mladic and Krstic? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then take you back to an answer which you gave a minute ago. I asked you whether Pandurevic had told you who had called that meeting. And your answer was: "He told me that a meeting was called by General Krstic." My question then was: "And not by General Mladic?" You then answered: "No, not General Mladic. It was Krstic." So a minute ago, you positively denied --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that Pandurevic had told that you Generals Krstic and Mladic had called for that meeting, and now approximately two minutes later, you tell us that that was not a truthful answer and that you stand by your previous answer, by your previous statement that the meeting was as Pandurevic had told you, was called by Generals Mladic and Krstic. Do you have any explanation for that inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm explaining the consistency or, rather, discrepancies because it was General Krstic who issued specific tasks for the use of those units, and the commander of the tactical group reported to General Krstic, i.e., the then-Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps. Therefore, reports can be submitted to the commander, i.e., the officer in charge of the operation at that moment. The presence of General Mladic was obvious. He was there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, earlier you told us, also a minute ago, that you had no knowledge about who attended that meeting. Now, 15 minutes later, you tell us that General Mladic was there as well. So apparently you do have knowledge about who attended. Any explanation for that inconsistency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, this is not an inconsistency. The way I understood the question was this: Which of the brigade commanders and participants in combat surrounding Srebrenica also participated in the debriefing at the command of the Bratunac Brigade. It was not only Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic who was there but also the other commanders of the units that had been engaged in combat. I don't know who was present. This would be my answer to the question that was put to me by Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. The question was, first, Mr. Stojanovic asked you: "Who attended that debriefing on the 11th of July in the evening at the command of the Bratunac Brigade?" Your answer was: "We did not discuss the debriefing."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm just putting to you what you said. Then a few lines further down: "Did he tell you anything about the participants of the debriefing? Who was there?" Your answer: "I don't know. He didn't tell me." If you consider all this not to be inconsistent, then we've heard your explanations until now. I leave it to that. We'll take a break and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. McCloskey, now being back in the viva voce modus, one hour was your estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My recollection it was one hour and a half. I think we matched the -- the -- the Defence, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it was initially on the famous schedule, it was one hour, but I do understand that we -- you have adjusted that or I don't know even know whether you were the source of the one hour but it's one hour and a half now. And I take it you will be able to finish within that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I certainly hope so. I don't intend on going much beyond the 12th of July, but we'll have to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the witness has an inclination to move away from the question. I'm confident that you're able to -- to guide him on the right track. And we will have a little bit of an earlier break because Judge Fluegge will not be with us during the very last session, so we'll take the next break at 1.15. Mr. Dragutinovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey. You find Mr. McCloskey to your right. Mr. McCloskey is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, you're testifying today that on the 12th of July, Vinko Pandurevic told you about what had gone on, somewhat, but at least he had told you about that meeting that had happened the night before, on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see at temporary page 29, line 17, you say: "Therefore, he told me that on the 11th in the evening and later during the night he had had a briefing or debriefing in the commands of the Bratunac Brigade and that he had returned very late and he had taken another route and he had travelled ..." So if we could go back to your signed statement that His Honour Judge Orie was speaking to you about, 1D1643, page 5, and we understand you corrected some things in this and -- though it's unclear to me exactly what, I want to ask you about something. Looking at paragraph 13, we see that you're talking about leaving with Pandurevic going towards Srebrenica. They say there was -- you say there was a typo on the dates. But explain this to me: In the middle of the page: "Well, Pandurevic left Srebrenica for Bratunac travelling via Potocari. He said he was going a meeting called by Generals Mladic and Krstic. He also said that the agenda of the meeting was to report on the combat operations completed and possibly to receive new tasks following the taking of Srebrenica." Later on, down in 14 he tells you: "The meeting was supposed to take place in the evening and Commander Pandurevic did not mention who was going to attend it." In your testimony, and frankly as you will know in our other testimonies, you're speaking of learning this about -- about this meeting in the past tense. In this statement, which you read and signed, you are talking about Pandurevic telling about a meeting he is going to, in the future. Now, isn't it correct, sir, that you did learn on the 12th of July that Pandurevic was going to a meeting in Bratunac with the commander, Krstic and Mladic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the question is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you did learn on the 12th of July that Pandurevic was going to a meeting in Bratunac, with Commander Krstic and Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned paragraph 13, but in paragraph 12, it says that I spent the night Zeleni Jadar. So that tallies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. McCloskey puts to you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- he says: Isn't it true that you learned on the 12th of July that Pandurevic was going to a meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Commander Pandurevic, on the 12th of July, Jadar-Srebrenica, on that road, I heard from him that he had already attended a meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now for the transcript it says the 1st but I think it's pretty essential -- oh, it's corrected. Yes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My question is: It's been a long time, many years, do you consider it reasonable that you heard about this meeting in the future tense, that Pandurevic was going to a meeting on the 12th July? And to be precisely clear that you, on the 12th of July, together with Pandurevic, that's when he told you he was going to a meeting in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No. Rather, in the vehicle, on the 12th in the morning, on the road, Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica he said to me that he had been at a meeting at a briefing in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we can all read your statement which clearly states it's the future. So you read that, you signed it, and that was just one big mistake or misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not give such a statement. Maybe my statement has been misinterpreted. I am sure that I have not given that kind of statement. What is true is that I heard about that from the commander in the vehicle on the road from Zeleni Jadar to Srebrenica that the previous night, he attended a meeting in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, there's something else you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could I seek full clarification. Is it your testimony that you learned about this meeting only on the morning of the 12th, or had something been said about it already on the 11th by Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Lieutenant-Colonel Pandurevic was in Zeleni Jadar on the 11th, he just intimated that he would be attending a briefing that evening. That is, the 11th, in the evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You also testified at temporary page 30, lines 21 through 25, that basically, "What I learned from the commander was that the debriefing was about previous combat activities and the future task which was established at that meeting and that was that the units were to be deployed in the Zepa sector to engage the Zepa Brigade and neutralise its members." Now, if we look at your statement that's still up on the screen, we don't see in paragraph 13 any mention of going to Zepa. In fact, at page 14 [sic], you say: "As I understood things I would say that it was obvious that the units of the 28th Division had withdrawn from Srebrenica town in order" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are reading, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "... in order not to sustain losses and that they will still -- and that they were still somewhere in the vicinity. The 28th Division had not been completely destroyed -- had not been destroyed completely and I presumed that a task would be issued to that effect at the meeting. Pandurevic had to attend on the orders of General Mladic and Krstic." Then we have the part about your presumptions about who was attending. Then we go on. And there's no mention of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That was not page 14, but paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Paragraph. Thank you, Your Honour. "The next day on 12 July Tactical Group 1 and Tactical Group 2 as well I believe were articulated with searching the terrain between Srebrenica and Viogor and Suceska. The commander gathered all members of the unit that is to say platoon commanders and said that everyone was to prepare their troops to march towards Suceska. The Podrinje detachment was there as well. We left around 1200 hours and arrived at the assigned position in the area of Viogor-Suceska at around 1500 hours." And we can see that what is in paragraph 16, where you were awaiting Krstic's orders there. Then we get to paragraph 17: "General Krstic arrived in our sector sometime in the afternoon, around 1700 or 1800 hours. Our commander, Pandurevic was there as well. General Krstic and he had a conversation and we were told that we do not need to go to Suceska that there were no 28th Division units there, that the division had gone further up north towards the village of Jaglici and that our unit was to spend the night there. At the meeting with Krstic, it was announced that our unit might be tasked with combat operations." We need to turn the page in the English. Thank you. And the B/C/S. "It was announced that our units might be tasked with combat operations in the area of Zepa ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So according to this statement, you don't hear anything about Zepa until the evening of 12 July, but now you have testified for the first time that you heard about this before that. How do you explain that important difference?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I explain it in the following way. The problem that -- that cropped up and that I hadn't stated before; namely, I heard that order from the commander to go to Zepa. Probably it was an oversight on my part, but I know before General Krstic arrived in the Viogor area the units from our tactical group learned that it was possible to go on mission to Zepa. That is to say, we knew about that. Then a problem cropped up in the tactical group itself. Actually combat group 2. This combat group 2 has a heterogenous composition --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Let me explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I don't have --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Do allow me to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have much time. It was a simple question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if Mr. McCloskey considers that you have either anticipated his question or that he wants to put the next question to you without having received an answer, he is free to do so. If, at the very end of your testimony there's anything you think we should know, then you can address us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: During --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: At the end or now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: During your stay here in The Hague, have you naturally seen or run into any former colleagues in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now? This time? In The Hague? Today? These couple of days? Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Three or four of them were all from the Army of Republika Srpska. I know some of them, and I don't know others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you see Milenko Jevdjevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I know Milenko Jevdjevic from before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether you had seen him during these days, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We could see each other during breakfast. We could see each other every day because we were at the same hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did he naturally speak to you about those events a bit, on those days when you were soldiers together?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: At the events where we took part together? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So did you talk with him about the period -- any -- any period between the 6th and the 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Some, yes; others, no. Just those when we could meet each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, you've just testified that you have not said -- you hadn't learned about the Zepa orders before, and you've testified that for the first time today. Is it not correct that Mr. Jevdjevic had kind of reminded you that that's what happened, that Mladic gave an order to go to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But you talked about that --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But you talked about that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Not about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What did you talk about in those days, the 12th/11th of July? What part of the story did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We mostly talked about our common acquaintances who were with us in the area of Zepa, the area of Srebrenica. And I did not go into his testimony because I am an elderly person now and all of this tires me out, and I didn't want to be filled with something that would make this stay more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I understand. He apparently wanted to talk you about it, and you took the better choice and didn't talk to him about it. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When did he want to talk to you about it? What day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No special day. At moments when he felt certain tension or something that he had experienced, something unpleasant in this courtroom. Just to make it easier upon himself to decompress without any tendency of leading me to some piece of information that I am absolutely aware of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But he told you a bit about what he was testifying about then.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: A bit, a bit, but not that much, since -- since his military occupation is signals and I have nothing to do with signals and communication, and I don't even understand all of that, if he were to tell me about all of that, I wouldn't even understand it. Like many other people would not understand it. Even here, in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I take it that he knew you were a witness in it case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you -- What makes you believe that people in this court -- in this courtroom would not understand these matters? Why do you think that's the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you said: "I don't even understand all of that," you were talking about signals. "If he were to tell me about all of that" --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said: "... like many other people would not understand it even here in this courtroom." What made you believe that people in this courtroom would not understand these signal matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only experts can understand communications and signals. This is a technical issue, and not even a civil engineer can talk on an equal footing with a mechanical engineer, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the only person I can discuss, my profession and my professional issues, is my colleague, a land surveyor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did Mr. Jevdjevic tell you that he had difficulties in explaining to us and that he experienced difficulties where people in this courtroom would not have understood him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When did you arrive in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hmm, on Monday, and the date was -- some ten days ago it was. Seven, eight days ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if I understand you well, part of your discussion included at least also the experience Mr. Jevdjevic has -- had in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be only logical for us to talk and exchange our experiences about the atmosphere in the courtroom, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, after he had concluded his testimony, did he add anything to what he may have said before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your conversations about what had happened in this courtroom were during the days or between the days in which he gave testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any time when we had free time to spend together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including over the last few days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Over the last few days, we did not talk. He was not in a mood for any kind of conversation about the courtroom. I think that he was not a mood to talk about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you also told us a minute ago that you told you a bit about his testimony and also that what he had experienced in this courtroom being unpleasant and also about our understanding, understanding of the persons in this courtroom, about the very technical nature of his -- of his answers. That's what I understood --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was just about communications, about his specialty. As for the rest, I think that the rest was understandable and anybody could understood him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So -- but did he then tell you because your answer is not entirely unambiguous in this respect, did he tell you that persons in this courtroom - I'm not specifying who that may have been - had difficulties in understanding the very technical matters about communication when he had explained that in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one additional short question. Did you see Mr. Jevdjevic yesterday after 1.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I saw him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the end of that question, is that it? No text? Can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am asking you if you saw Mr. Jevdjevic yesterday after 1.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only later I saw him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: When did you see -- "later" is after 1.00. When did you see him yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometime around 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We had an agreement to go somewhere and have a drink because he was leaving. It was to be by way of saying good-bye to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Nothing about the testimony of Mr. Jevdjevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You will recall your interview with the OTP on the 18th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you did not tell the OTP at that point about learning of the meeting between Pandurevic, Mladic and Krstic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's true, no one did ask you. But you didn't mention it yourself either, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of my interview, I was asked whether I would add something. I said that I answered all the questions and any additional answer of mine would have been groundless.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then on the 11th of June, 2007, you came here to testify. You were a Prosecution witness in the Popovic case, and you met with the OTP lawyer, Kweku Vanderpuye. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to a -- a brief account of your meeting with Mr. Vanderpuye; 65 ter 32122. Now at that meeting with Mr. Vanderpuye you didn't tell him about hearing there was an order from Mladic to go to Zepa from that meeting, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if the question was asked. I'm sure that I answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's look at it. Let's go to page 2 in both languages. And looking at bullet point -- what's 5. "The witness states that on 11 July Pandurevic attended a meeting in Bratunac. At that meeting, the witness assumes that General Mladic, corps commanders as well as commanders of the tactical group [sic] were present." "The witness states that on 12 July 1995, he was picked up by Pandurevic at the medical unit in Zeleni Jadar. Pandurevic drove him to Gostilj where a meeting was held among the commands of the tactical group. On the way there and while there, Pandurevic briefly told the witness about his prior meeting in Bratunac on the night of the 11th ... the witness states that Pandurevic told him that the meeting involved General Krstic but did not mention others present and involved the future operations of ... tactical groups, including searching the terrain for Muslim units leaving Srebrenica towards Suceska. The witness indicates that Pandurevic told him that on his way back from this meeting he took the route back to Srebrenica through Sase in order to avoid what he described as a mass of people. "On 12 July sometime before noon an order to conduct combat operations in Suceska was issued. The tactical group commanded by Pandurevic took on a support role for the other tactical group commanded by Trivic (which was in a combat posture)." Now, we can see what's said in paragraph 7 briefly. Paragraph 8 is when you talk again as you had -- we'd seen previous: "Later around 17 to 1800 hours an informal meeting was held at Viogor at which General Krstic was present. At this time Krstic informed that the operations in Suceska would no longer be carried out --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need to turn the page, I believe, in the B/C/S. "As reconnaissance had shown ... the Muslim units were no longer there. The tactical group was directed to await further orders. Subsequently, the meeting continued more formally as a meeting among the commands of Pandurevic's group prepares were in anticipation of the next phase of the operations which the witness states that the group command believed to involve Zepa."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, again, we see in this information, you don't mention learning about Zepa from the command meeting. You don't learn about it until the evening of 12 July. That's a correct account of what you told Mr. Vanderpuye, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, you basically say something similar when you testify a few days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to 65 ter 32114. Let's go to page 24. This is Mr. Vanderpuye leading you on -- in direct examination. We're now -- we see that we're on the 12th. "Q. All right. This next morning can you tell us what happened. This is the morning of the 12th. "A. On the morning of the 12th, I already knew that our units had entered Srebrenica because the commander arrived in Zeleni Jadar where the logistics of our unit was positioned. He was on some assignment and he also went to see me, so when he finished his business, I returned together with the commander to Srebrenica." It goes down. Mr. Vanderpuye asks you if you discuss anything and you answer on line 15: "Yes, we talked. We talked about the things that happened after I was sent to Zeleni Jadar, how the units entered Srebrenica, and all the things that transpired until we met up again. "Q. And can you recall specifically what the commander told you? "A. Well, he was saying that at the outset there was some resistance from the 28th Division, but it was practically non-existent the end so that our units entered Srebrenica without encountering any resistance, that the tactical group entered the town, the units were stationed in surrounding buildings to secure the units that were in Srebrenica. After that, he had gone to Bratunac on the Srebrenica-Potocari-Bratunac road. Now I'm coming to the part I wanted to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We need to turn the page. "Did he mention to you why he went to Bratunac? "He went to a meeting that was convened by General Mladic and General Krstic. "Q. And did he mention to you what was discussed at the meeting? "A. To submit reports on missions accomplished and missions that might follow after ... taking of Srebrenica. "Q. Okay. Did he mention to you what missions might follow after this [sic] taking of Srebrenica at this time [sic]. "A. Well, from what I understand [sic] it was evident that the units of the 28th Division had retreated from Srebrenica but they only pulled out of the town. So that [sic] there was combat in prospect to the west of the town because the units of the 28th Division were still there. They had not been crushed. And that was probably going to determine our next assignments." Now that answer, sir, that you gave is the position of the Prosecution. That was the situation you were in. Do you stand by that statement that I just read to you, the -- those last five lines.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then we go on. And did he mention what time this meeting was? "A. I'm not sure. It was some time in the evening. Or at night. "Q. And other than commanders General Mladic, General Krstic, Commander Pandurevic, did he mention who else was at the meeting. "A. I don't remember. I suppose there were other unit commanders, commanders of units of tactical group strength or brigade strength. I can only suppose but I really don't remember the names." Then we -- he asked you on the bottom of the page what happened while you were in Gostilj. You say on the next page that you were awaiting assignments. I'm going through it a bit more briefly. "And did these new orders come at some point?" In line 4. And you say: "Yes, they did. Tactical Group 1 was ordered to be prepared as backup for Tactical Group 2 which was going to search the terrain, as the terminology went, on the axis of Srebrenica-Viogor village-Suceska village." And later on, we see that you talk about the troops gathering and start moving towards Suceska. In line 20, you say: "We start moving with the commander in his vehicle in the direction of Srebrenica, Viogor, Suceska and we started it was around 1200 hours and we reached our destination at around 1400 hours and maybe 1500 hours." If we go on, we'll see that as we get to the afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page. I would go to page 28. And this is where you're telling what is now should be familiar to us, that around 1700 hours or maybe 1800 hours the Chief of Staff arrived in the Viogor section. That's General Krstic, right, the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just saw that. Okay let me go on. And then, as we see, the -- General Krstic -- you say: "General Krstic had a conversation with the commander and during that conversation he made us understand that in the Suceska sector there were no units of the 28th Division and that this division had moved in order in the direction of Jaglici village and that we should keep our unit in the Viogor sector and that we should prepare our units [sic] to spend the night." We go down with a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You missed the last word.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: "The night there." Excuse me, "the night there." Thank you. And then I'll skip a question or two. Mr. Vanderpuye says: "Did you -- did you have any indication as do what your unit was supposed to do next or could you [sic] expect to do next following General Krstic's visit. "A. There were indications that we would prepare our units to proceed with combat activities in the Zepa sector." So there again I think it is now perhaps the third time you don't learn about Zepa until the evening of 12 July. Yet after speaking to Mr. Jevdjevic - and I don't know what was said or if anything was said - you come into this court and testify for the first time that you learned from the 11 July meeting that Zepa was the main operation. How is it, sir, that it's the first time today in 2015 that we hear this from you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: This claim that I learned that from Jevdjevic is wrong. Secondly, and you're not allowing me to say this, I'm instructed that I should say it at the end but I should say it now, with your leave. And this would give you the explanation as to how come I remember Zepa now and not before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it is directly related to that question, you may briefly explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the briefest possible way, we knew about Zepa already on the 12th, in the morning. We had a lot of problems with Combat Group 2. They were not mentally and physically prepared to go to the Zepa sector because on the previous few days it had seven dead and one missing. There were even 15 missing in action at some point. Already that morning they wanted to be replaced by another unit because apparently they did not have either the mental or physical strength to participate in combat in the Zepa sector. That's why I don't understand how come I didn't mention that. But I know that that was one of the reasons why we spent the entire afternoon on the 12th only improving the morale and physical and mental condition of Combat Group 2 we didn't want to ask for replacement. We didn't want any other unit to be brought in from the Zvornik Brigade. We wanted to prepare our unit for the task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think it's break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is break time. We'd like to see you back there 20 minutes, Mr. Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Judge Fluegge, is for urgent personal reasons, unable to continue to hear this case for the next 38 minutes. He'll be back tomorrow with us. Judge Moloto and myself have decided that it's in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case today. Therefore, we will sit under Rule 15 bis. There's another matter I'd just like to briefly address. The testimony that was read to the witness in -- which he has given in 2007 seems to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to put the announcement that Pandurevic would visit a meeting on that same 12th of July, if I see the sequence well. If -- first of all, if my understanding is wrong but I try to read the portion that is uploaded into e-court, if that impression is wrong, I'd like to hear. If the impression is right, then I at least would like to know whether anywhere in cross-examination the witness distances himself from any of what he said in the examination-in-chief by Mr. Vanderpuye. But please proceed, for the time being, Mr. McCloskey, because I think it would be inappropriate to further discuss the matter in the presence of the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, I -- I want, with a couple of, questions, sort of set the scene of where we are militarily on the 11th of July and the morning of the 12th. NATO has bombed on the 11th of July. You were injured; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The tactical group was able to go into Srebrenica on the early evening hours of 11 July and basically deploy near Gostilj, which is the -- the football pitch in Srebrenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a bit below the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And by the evening of 11 July, did the -- does the command that you were part of have any knowledge where the Muslims are? The Muslim army, I should say, the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where -- where -- where does the command think the Muslims are on the evening of 11 July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Since I was not in the command on the 11th of July, I could not have had an opportunity to be present during the assessment as to where the units of the 28th Division could be. That is to say, I'm not aware of this assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. But by the morning of the 12 July when you get back with the command, you learn that it's the command's feeling or knowledge that the Muslim 28th Division has fled in the direction or in the area of Suceska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The assessment was that it concentrated in the area of the village of Suceska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the VRS forces did not control anything but the Srebrenica town area and the area below that, between Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Also on the left, almost to Viogor, the village of Bajramovici where there were parts of Tactical Group 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Srebrenica, Zeleni Jadar, over to Bajramovici but in the area of Potocari, that area was still held by the Dutch forces, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Where the Dutch forces were I personally did not see that, and I don't know. Just from some conversations, I know that they were in Potocari. As for deployment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So by the evening of the 11th of July, NATO is still a threat, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening hours, no; in the afternoon hours, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: NATO air power was still -- could still be used against Serb forces on the 11th or 12th, could they not? And I mean from your position on the ground. You had to worry about NATO bombing you again, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So if, on the 11th of July, the Muslims are not in Srebrenica town. They're in the direction of Suceska. The majority of the enclave up to Potocari and beyond westward is not in VRS control. NATO is still a threat. It makes no sense militarily for General Mladic to issue an order to prepare troops to march to Zepa on the 11th of July, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't go into Commander Mladic's thinking. I can only think about my own level of thinking, that of a major. Anything beyond that would be pointless.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, from a major's position, then, that has many lives under his control, would it make sense to send the VRS troops, the hundreds of men deployed in Srebrenica and Zeleni Jadar, the next day, on to Zepa, when NATO's still a threat. You don't -- the Muslims are in the western of the enclave, uncontrolled. The Dutch still hold Potocari. As a major, makes no sense to issue that order at that time, does it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: At some moment it does make sense for a simple reason, because the units of the 28th Division, quite simply, let the town go. In my view, they left the population at somebody's mercy, which means that they withdrew as deep as possible into the territory or, rather, the enclave, with certain intentions that in my assessment had no combat intention or, rather, no intention to attack units of the Army of Republika Srpska that were attacking Srebrenica. Because from intercepted conversations during the attack on Srebrenica, the commanders themselves, the commanders of the units of the 28th Division, were in total disarray, in disagreement, what to do, whether to withdraw or not, where to assemble, we knew all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. One last time: We know your intelligence told you that the 28th Division had up to 10 to 15.000 able-bodied men, about a third of which were armed. If they are talking a stand in Suceska west of Srebrenica - and we'll get a map in a minute - and with all the other factors I explained, it makes no military sense for a major at that point to have all his troops go off to Zepa, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. I think that the witness has responded to that question. It is in the first sentence of the answer to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer this question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm go to object at this point. Asking the same question or a similar question twice is okay in cross-examination, especially when you're not getting much of an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness asked whether he may answer that question once again. And he is allowed to do so. The objection is denied. Mr. Stojanovic, in cross-examination the simple line question add, question answered, is not always applicable, and insistence on again an answer to the same question is, under certain circumstances, admissible. Therefore, Witness, you may answer the question again. Well, please do so. Whether it makes sense or not for a major.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Our assessment from my point of view and from the point of view of the higher command was that the 28th Division, quite simply, did not have the strength to put up any kind of resistance any longer, irrespective of the strength that you refer to, that's a bit exaggerated. So the resistance of the 28th Division over the following days became evident, and that is, that they were not able to resist the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I agree over the following days it did. In fact, on the afternoon of 12 July as you had stated in one of your previous statements, it became -- the VRS became aware, as you did, that the 28th Division had largely fled the enclave from the area of Jaglici and, at the same time, Potocari had been taken by the VRS and the MUP. And so the night of the 12th of July is a much different situation than the night of the 11th of July and makes much more sense in order to issue an order to Zepa for the 13th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a very complex question, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From your point of view, yes. It's a bit complex but from your point of view that's the way it seems. But from our military point of view, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, your question was pretty compound. And it seems that we are focussing more and more on what makes sense either for a major or for a general, or perhaps even common sense. Military sense, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, the reason I believe that you have never mentioned orders from General Mladic on the 11th of July before was because you spent the 12th of July marching in combat formation to find the Muslims in Suceska, and you knew it made no military sense to receive an order on the 11th of July and tell -- for some reason this testimony you have now come up with receiving an order from Mladic on -- or that you've told of an order of Mladic on the 11th of July. That's my point here. It's all coming back to the 11th of July and what you received. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: You're not right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to a map, we can help maybe get oriented a bit. It shouldn't take too long. P01087. And it's page 14 of the book and if I could, sir, I want to give you a miniature of this map because it's a map that was taken from the Zvornik Brigade and you'll notice, I think, that your name is on the bottom of it. It's hard -- if I can give a physical copy -- it's a little hard to see the whole one from the computer screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you'll get a hard copy. It should be shown first, unless Mr. Stojanovic ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps for us we can zero in on the right bottom corner where there should be some names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, sir, for -- for us that don't read Cyrillic, do you see your name down there in the right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's -- the name above you is -- give us the name and what's above you? You see Mihajlo Galic there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Major Mihajlo Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And below Galic, it says what?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Major Dragutinovic. Major Dragutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you -- if can you remember, can you just tell us a bit about this -- this map that was -- was retrieved from the Zvornik Brigade in 1998 in a search? For example, is it an account of the battles afterward, or is it a -- an account of the battles before, or during or -- or what?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the dates are the 1st of September, 1992 to the end of December. You can see it in the left-hand side corner, and it says "working map of the operations department."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and we have a translated version of that on the next page, but I don't think we need worry about that. What I -- what's the purpose of this map? What is this map designed to depict? For example, we see blue and red around the Srebrenica enclave area, and we see blue and red along what is the front line area. Can you just give us a little background on this map. What is it, what's it depicting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of this map is to provide an outline of the participation and activities of the Zvornik Brigade at a certain point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And does that include the -- what the -- how the Zvornik Brigade was deployed and the directions they went in during the Srebrenica operation that you've been describing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the left part. This is the defence line of the Zvornik Brigade. It partly goes all the way to Vlasenica, Milici, Sekovici, in the direction of Doboj. This is a rather generalised map. And in the right-hand side corner, you can see the contours of a line depicting activities around Srebrenica and the enclave itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to a blow-up of one section. It should be page 16. If we could ... here we go. And if we could bring it down a little bit so we can get the north of the map. Perhaps that's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The blue circle in the north of the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we blow that up a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we can now see the village of Jaglici that is within the general boundaries of that more oval than circle and a feature called Milacevici. What is that oval, blue marking, what is that designed to depict?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness needs to come to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, witness, could you come -- could you speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. This is it the general sector of withdrawal of the 28th Division from the Suceska sector towards the northern part of the enclave into the Jaglici and Milacevici villages sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you take a pen and write just a circle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Witness, you'll be provided with a pen with which you can write on the screen. But wait for a second. The usher will assist you. And do not start marking anything before you have received clear instructions to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you study the map a bit, find where Suceska is noted. As you mentioned to us, you are a surveyor, a geometra [phoen]. Do you see where Suceska is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just put an oval around the feature of Suceska.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And you've also mentioned the feature of Bojne. Could you ... well, you missed the B but that's going to have be close enough.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And now can you -- you've also mentioned Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we look carefully, we can see -- you've got the V and the i of Viogor, which is written in large letters, vertically on the map.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Viogor is bigger, but this is a sector of the deployment of the tactical group along the Srebrenica-Milici road. And it suffices for me to just show you where Tactical Group 1 was. I believe that this was enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now the red arrows that we see, we see them protruding from the south of the map going north across Bojne and Srebrenica. Does that reflect the axis of the -- of the movement of those troops?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the upper part of the map, according to our task, the line that we were supposed to reach was the line that I encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At Bojne?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Bojne.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the red lines that are going due west on the map towards Suceska, is that the area that you and your unit, Tactical Group 1, were taking on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, this is the axis that was used by both Tactical Group 1 and 2 to move along the road Srebrenica-Viogor-Milici old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Did you draw this or -- is that why your name's on it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Probably. If my name's there, then it will be me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so this red arrow in the north of the map that is coming down from a village called Borici through to Potocari, that reflects the movement, that reflects the movement [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... of the Serb forces on -- that took the Potocari area; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, that was the task of a unit. I can't remember which one. That's why I just outlined that another unit would be in charge of that task. I -- even didn't put its name on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Map marked by the witness would receive, Madam Registrar, number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map would receive P7148.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could we go to 65 ter 04287.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could show the Serbian version of this for the witness and perhaps leave the big one up so he can get a view of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, you may recall seeing this before but it's from the Zvornik Brigade command and it's for July. And we can see that in the -- in the translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey was asking for having the B/C/S version exclusively on the screen. Yes. And now could it be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: May be a bit hard to make out but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you looking for the witnesses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We should see number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could you just briefly tell us what this is? We see it's for Juli 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness needs to move to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you asked to [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In that case I won't see anything on the screen. It's too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. The usher would assist in re-directing the microphone in such a way that you can both see it and that can you be heard as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This records presence of manpower in the Zvornik Brigade. The purpose of this is to check the engagement of the manpower, and I can see my name under number 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I need. I'd like to offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I don't understand what all these markings mean. I'm not quite sure I understand the purpose now of tendering this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, can we --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you explain to us briefly what these markings mean, how it relates to attendance ...

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, where you see pluses, that means that the person was present in the unit. Letter T means that the person is in the unit but somewhere on a mission in the field. A C means that the person is on furlough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've got a T in black and a T in red. Can you explain the difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No difference at all. People used different pens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can we go to the English, please, and keep that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You tendered it. I heard of no objections. Apparently it's -- it will be further explained, Mr. -- you'll further explore this evidence, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. There's a legend in -- on page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have a look at that then to see what is explained us to there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's -- let's go to page 3 before we go to 4, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So, sir, in English, we see abbreviations and an explanation for who they are, what they mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could -- I believe it's page 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I may be wrong about that. I apologise. All right. I understand. Those are noted on the main page and we have just for simplicity noted what they are. And these are the people and some of their assignments and abbreviations for the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I can see the month of July written on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could get rid of the English and just blow up the big one again. And in the -- the middle of the page, is that -- describes very initials that mean various things, positions, ranks, et cetera; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, this will just help us in the future in identifying the people and where they are as the story unfolds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for 04287 will be P7150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7150 is admitted -- let me just check. P7150 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could now go to 65 ter 30229.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And as we're waiting for that to come up, sir, have you occasionally been the duty officer at the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that's going to be hard for you to read, but, yeah, hopefully you can make it out. It's from the command of the Drina Corps dated 7 March 1995. It is entitled: Signals table. And it's to the 5th Mixed Artillery Regiment Command, and it says: "We're sending you attached a table of signals in the Drina Corps PVO, which is an anti-aircraft defence system, called Grabovica." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that but I don't see a link to myself at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's read the next sentence. It says: "This signals table is to be used for communicating via communications equipment only among the duty operations centre of the Drina Corps and the duty officer in the brigades (independent battalions)." And we can see it says: "Brigade (independent battalion) commands will produce their own signals tables for command work in the PVO system with their subordinate unit." Then it says: "The Grabovica signals table comes into effect on 10 March 1995 at 1400 hours." As a duty officer, did you have to be aware of this kind of a signals information?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Every duty officer should have a signals table. And these signals tables are used whenever there is an imminent air-strike, which was announced, or things like that. This serves to instruct the units to prepare for defence, to be on alert, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right, I'd offer this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 30229 receives number 7151.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7151 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: One last related document and I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are over the time already. But if it would conclude this portion then perhaps, if you move to a totally different subject, with the indulgence of those who are assisting us, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter 30230.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Sir, this is my understanding that this was the table that was attached to this letter. And is this the kind of thing that you would have been familiar with? We can see that there's various statements, such as in number 8, "attack on aerial targets, forbidden." And then it says one to ten, "Bura", then 11 to 21, "Cer," and then 22 to 31, "Golub". Does this mean that during those various dates of July there's a different code-name for not attacking aerial targets?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: You can see yourself that from a certain time to a certain time, codes, i.e., names, were changed. From a certain point in time to another point in time the code-name would be "sun" and from 11 to 22 would be "night" and then "cloud." Therefore, those signals would be used either for the launch of action or for any other thing. As a matter of fact, that is anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: This is in favour of protecting corps units, i.e., brigade units, and their troops from possible air-strikes. Let's not even mention whose air force would that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is a good place to stop. I will offer it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 30230 receives number P7152.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Witness, we'll adjourn for the day but not until after I have instructed you that you should not speak to anyone or communicate with whomever, not at breakfast, not at lunch, not at 5.00 p.m., with whomever about your testimony. That includes how you have experienced your presence in court when giving your testimony. Is that clear to you, that you should not in any way communicate with whomever about anything related to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may now follow the usher. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I re-read the portion of the 2007 testimony, and I think I was a bit confused by the word sometimes "was" sometimes "had been," and that I may have changed my understanding on where the conversations between Pandurevic and the witness are the subject of the testimony and when it was about the meeting, re-reading it, it makes clear to me that it was conversation about what had happened the previous day, that is, at least the content of the testimony again in 2007. So, therefore, my request to report if there would be any change in cross-examination is not applicable any further. We adjourn for the day and after having thanked all those assisting us, we adjourn until tomorrow, Thursday, the 26th of February, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 26th day of February, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
